strands.subStrand: Interactive Speaking (2 sessions)  Greetings in formal contexts  Non-verbal cues
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify basic greetings in formal contexts, b) apply non-verbal cues that show active listening for effective communication, c) appreciate the need for active listening for effective communication.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● listen to a conversation on greetings in formal situations, ● pick out words and phrases used to express greetings in formal contexts e.g. (assalamu alaykum, sabahal khayr, masala khayr, maa ismuka?, keyfa haaluka?” anaa masruurun biliqaika. shukran)  respond to formal greetings while applying non-verbal cues (i.e. facing the speaker, maintaining eye contact, gestures and facial expressions),  work jointly to role play formal greetings in formal settings using non- verbal cues,  practice using polite language in a conversation using words (i.e. May I
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why should we use polite language when interacting with others?

strands.subStrand: Listening for Information (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building  Paraphrasing key ideas
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information, b) paraphrase key ideas from an oral text for information, c) appreciate the roles of extended family members.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● listen to an audio recording based on the family, ● work with peers to pick out names of nuclear and extended family members from the recording, ● team up to paraphrase key ideas on nuclear and extended family members from an oral text, ● role play the various members of the nuclear and extended family with peers.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why should we listen attentively?

strands.subStrand: Active Listening (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building  Description (adjectives-size and colour)
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify animals (pets, farm and wild animals) for information, b) describe animals based on their size and colour, c) acknowledge the role that animals play in the environment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● watch an audio-visual recording about animals and birds, ● work jointly to identify the animals and birds from the recording, ● list the vocabulary on flashcards and organise in a class portfolio, ● collaborate with peers to describe the animals based on their colour and size, ● team up with peers to prepare a mosaic of a farm animal of choice, ● display the mosaic during the art exhibition and interclass contests.
strands.inquiryQuestions: What are the strategies of active listening?

strands.subStrand: Oral Expression (2 sessions)  Sequencing ideas  Non-verbal cues
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline activities carried out on a daily basis at home in their order of sequence, b) apply non-verbal cues to make a presentation on daily routines at home, c) appreciate the need for confidence and clarity in oral expression for lifelong learning.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● observe their daily routine and make entries in a diary, ● organise the activities carried out in a day in order of sequence, ● work jointly to make a presentation of daily home routines while using appropriate non-verbal cues, ● peer assess each other’s use of non-verbal cues for constructive feedback.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is it important to keep a routine? 2. How do non- verbal cues support oral communication?

strands.subStrand: Interactive Speaking (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building  Expressing intention- I will..., I plan to...
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) name fun activities that can be enjoyed at specific times, b) use target words to express intention of taking part in an action, c) appreciate interacting and speaking for effective communication.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● listen attentively to an audio presentation about making plans and setting appointments, ● identify various fun activities one may enjoy and set plans for, ● role-play a dialogue about making plans and appointments using target words e.g. - “Are you available next week?”; - Are you free on the 20th? - “I am sorry I won’t be able to see the doctor today, - can you please book me for tomorrow at 09:30?”
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does interacting with others help in language acquisition?

strands.subStrand: Oral Expression (2 sessions)  Polite language (etiquette)  Vocabulary building
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify a range of words used to express etiquette, b) apply polite language in a conversation for effective communication, c) develop interest in using polite language in communication for co- existence.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● team up to identify a range of words used to express etiquette in the restaurant, ● list the etiquette words on charts and display on the language corner, ● use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in make sentences using the target words, ● identify particles (harf) from given sentences and pronounce them correctly ● work jointly to role play a restaurant setting to apply polite language and etiquette.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How do you identify harf (particles) in a sentence?

strands.subStrand: Listening for Information (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the various states of health for information, b) describe the various states of health from an oral text, c) develop interest in listening to oral Arabic texts for enjoyment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● listen to an audio recording on states of health e.g. sick, tired, unwell, satisfied, energetic, ● work jointly to identify the various vocabulary from the audio recording, ● listen and pronounce particles (harf) correctly, ● team up to dramatize a short play on visiting the doctor, ● ask and answer questions using the correct pronunciation and intonation, ● describe the various states of health presented in the role play.
strands.inquiryQuestions: What do you consider when listening for information?

strands.subStrand: Active Listening (2 sessions)  Summarising key ideas
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline key aspects to consider when listening to an oral text related to the theme, b) summarize key ideas from an oral text given for comprehension, c) develop interest in active listening for effective comprehension of language.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● collaborate with peers to identify key considerations when listening to a text related to theme, ● watch a video presentation and identify different activities people carry out in relation to weather and environment, ● work jointly to summarise the key ideas from the recording related to theme, ● use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in describing activities carried out in their locality. e.g. farming, fishing, rearing animals, trading etc.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does a poor listening habit affect your communication?

strands.subStrand: Interactive Speaking (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building  Giving instructions
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline words used to give directions for effective communication, b) give instructions on direction to a locality for effective communication, c) appreciate the need for clarity of instruction for effective communication.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● listen attentively to an audio presentation on directions to a given locality, ● list words used to ask or give directions on flashcards e.g. turn, go, cross, - left, right, ahead, cardinal points, ● team up to give instructions to peers to a given place, ● work jointly to play a language game involving giving and asking for directions to a place e.g. treasure hunt game ● listen and respond to instructions given by peers on the following directions, e.g. turn right, turn left, go straight, stop etc.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we ensure that the instructions we give are always clear and complete?

strands.subStrand: Reading Fluency (2 sessions)  Reading speed  Intonation  Particles (harf)
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a text on formal greetings and introduction, b) apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency, c) develop interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● read short sentences on formal greetings while observing the correct pronunciation of words, ● collaborate with peers to circle the particles (harf) in sentences, ● work jointly to read a dialogue on formal greeting and introduction between two people or groups using appropriate speed and intonation,
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you ensure fluency in reading?

strands.subStrand: Reading Fluency (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building- extended family members  Stress  Intonation  Particles (harf)
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify target words and phrases from a written text, b) use appropriate stress and intonation for fluency, c) appreciate the role of fluency for language acquisition.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  read texts and underline words and phrases related to nuclear and extended family members,  work jointly to read simple sentences and circle particles (harf) in sentences,  take turns reading a short conversation about nuclear and extended family members using appropriate stress and intonation,  peer assess each other’s reading for fluency.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you show love to your family members? 2. Why should we read fluently?

strands.subStrand: Reading for Comprehension (2 sessions)  Reading pace  Comprehension questions
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a short text fluently and at a good pace, b) respond to questions from a text based on the theme, c) appreciate reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  work with peers to read a short text on animals fluently,  collaborate with peers to conduct a speed reading game and identify the best speed to read at,  peer assess each other’s performance for fluency,  work jointly to respond to direct and inferential questions from the texts read.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you extract specific information from a text?

strands.subStrand: Reading Fluency: Pronunciation (2 sessions)  Particles (harf)  Speed
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read simple words with correct pronunciation of particles (harf) for fluency, b) apply appropriate speed when reading a text for fluency, c) develop interest in reading Arabic texts.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● engage in reading short sentences on routine and schedules, ● identify vocabulary and phrases related to the theme, ● work jointly to read the identified words while focusing on correct pronunciation of particles (harf), ● apply appropriate speed for fluency, ● read text of their interest independently during free time.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you improve your pace when reading Arabic?

strands.subStrand: Reading for Information (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building  Inferring meaning
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify vocabulary from a text for comprehension, b) infer meaning of vocabulary for effective communication, c) embrace vocabulary building for language acquisition.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● read texts aloud about making plans and appointments for fun activities, ● work with peers to pick out vocabulary from the text, ● build a vocabulary bank based on words identified, ● work jointly to infer the meaning of vocabulary from context, ● confirm the meaning of the words from a print or online dictionary, ● team up to play a language game involving matching vocabulary to their meaning, ● team up with peers in class to prepare a planning record for fun activities.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is it good to make plans before carrying out an activity? 2. How can we find meaning of new words in a text?

strands.subStrand: Reading for Information (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building- foods and drinks  Relating events to real life
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify vocabulary items in a text for comprehension, b) relate events and characters in a text to real life, c) develop interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● read texts with vocabulary and phrases aloud on ordering food in restaurants using appropriate pronunciation, ● pick out vocabulary related to the theme and list them on charts for display, ● work jointly to make comparison between events and characters in texts and real life, ● team up with peers to research on different types of foods and drinks and list them, ● work jointly to organise the list in the class portfolio.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How do poor reading habits affect learning?

strands.subStrand: Reading Aloud: Dialogue (2 sessions)  Characters  Reading speed and accuracy
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify characters in a dialogue for information, b) apply appropriate speed and accuracy in reading a dialogue, c) develop interest in reading variety of texts for language acquisition.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● read a dialogue with peers, ● work with peers to discuss the characters in the dialogue, ● prepare a mind map to show how the characters relate to each other from the dialogue, ● conduct a reader’s theatre to read a dialogue at appropriate speed and with accuracy, ● work jointly to answer questions based on the dialogue, ● engage in reading activities for fluency and understanding with assistance from parents/guardians.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is reading important?

strands.subStrand: Reading for Information: Visuals (2 sessions)  Interpreting visuals  Summarising texts
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify visuals representing information related to the theme, b) summarise a text into a visual for comprehension, c) develop interest in reading short Arabic texts.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● work jointly to pick visuals representing information based on weather and the environment, ● discuss the visuals and the information they carry, ● work jointly to summarise a text into a visual related to the theme, ● share their work with peers for peer assessment, ● team up to prepare a mosaic on a creative idea related to the weather and environment.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How do visuals pass information? 2. Why is it said that a picture is worth a thousand words?

strands.subStrand: Extensive Reading: Library Skills (2 sessions)  Identifying reading materials  Tracking reading progress
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify resources from a collection of materials for reading, b) track reading progress for lifelong learning, c) develop a positive attitude towards reading.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  work jointly to discuss factors to consider when identifying resources from a wider collection of materials,  conduct a silent reading session with peers to read grade appropriate Arabic materials,  prepare a reading log to track their reading progress. Include details on: - title of the material - author - number of pages - key events - characters in the text - date of access.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we ensure we pick interesting reading materials easily and fast?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 sessions)  Reordering jumbled sentences  Coherence  Sequencing
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) organise ideas coherently for effective communication b) compose a well sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly, c) develop interest in writing Arabic.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  team up to construct simple sentences on formal greeting to express their feelings,  reorganise jumbled up sentences to form a meaningful paragraph,  use a digital device to play a digital language game involving dragging and dropping sentences to form complete and coherent paragraphs,  compose a well sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is greeting important? 2. How does lack of sequence affect meaning of texts?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing: Handwriting (2 sessions)  Good handwriting  Arabic writing style
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify features of a good Arabic handwriting for information, b) create a well written story using the Arabic writing style, c) develop interest in writing Arabic.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● work jointly to identify features of a good Arabic handwriting, ● list the features on a chart for display, ● work jointly to create a well written story based on the theme, ● share their write-ups for peer assessment, ● team up to conduct a writing contest to hone their Arabic writing skills, ● publish the best written compositions in the school or public children’s magazine.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is it good to write clearly?

strands.subStrand: Guided writing (2 sessions)  Vocabulary building- animals and birds  Simple sentences
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) outline vocabulary related to animals and birds for comprehension, b) construct simple sentences on a given context correctly, c) appreciate the skills of writing for effective communication.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  work jointly to discuss the vocabulary related to the theme on animals and birds in the surrounding,  collaborate to build a vocabulary bank on words related to animals and birds and organise it in the class portfolio,  team up to match vocabulary to their meaning,  collaborate with peers to complete sentences with words on animals,  write simple sentences about animals and share with their peers for review.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you improve your writing skills in Arabic? 2. How does vocabulary help in Arabic language learning?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing (2 sessions)  Diary keeping
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) sequence activities in relation to time of occurrence, b) organise activities in a diary for effective planning, c) appreciate the planning skills for lifelong learning.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● observe the school routine and write simple sentences, ● collaborate to organise the key events in the school into a well sequenced account of school activities, ● work together to prepare a diary to record school activities, ● team up with peers to fill the events in the diary, ● work jointly to discuss the benefit of planning events beforehand.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you manage your time well?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition (2 sessions)  Simple sentences  Imaginative composition- 3 paragraphs
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension, b) create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension, c) appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● work jointly to construct sentences using vocabulary related to making plans and appointments, ● collaborate with peers in rearranging jumbled up words to make meaningful sentences, ● use a substitution table to form meaningful sentences and share with peers, ● create a personal imaginative composition using the vocabulary identified in the theme, ● share their best written composition on the class gallery, ● conduct interclass writing contests to write essays and imaginative compositions.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can one develop a creative story?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing: Summary Writing (2 sessions)  Key ideas  Summarising
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline key ideas from a text for information, b) summarise a text for information, c) appreciate summary writing as a strategy for knowledge preservation.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● work jointly to read a text related to the theme on foods and drinks- kitchen utensils, ● prepare a mind map to list the key ideas from a text, ● team up to discuss what should be considered when writing summaries, ● summarise the text into fewer words (80 words), ● peer review their summarised work for improvement.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why do we keep our utensils clean? 2. How can we reduce a text without leaving out key ideas?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing: Poems (2 sessions)  Simple sentences  Simple poem
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary, b) compose a simple poem for comprehension, c) develop interest in artistic expression through writing.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● listen to an audio recording and write vocabulary related to the theme, ● form sentences using descriptive words and vocabulary identified to express their health states, e.g. I am sick today etc. ● share sentences with their peers for review, ● work jointly to compose a poem related to different health states using identified thematic vocabulary, ● team up to stage their well written poem during the interclass competition.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you write an interesting poem?

strands.subStrand: Guided writing (2 sessions)  Key ideas  Imaginative composition
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) gather key ideas from a text related to the theme, b) compose an imaginative composition for comprehension, c) embrace creative writing for enjoyment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● watch a video presentation and identify different activities people carry out in different weather conditions and environment, ● work jointly to outline the key points from the video presentation, ● observe picture displays and identify different activities people carrying out, ● based on the pictures, compose an imaginative composition, ● share the compositions with peers for constructive review, ● share the best written compositions in the school or children’s magazine.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we make a composition interesting?

strands.subStrand: Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility (2 sessions)  Essays  Characteristics of a good essay
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the characteristics of a good written piece, b) compose an essay on the locating school facilities neatly and legibly, c) develop positive attitude towards writing Arabic.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  discuss the characteristics of a well and neatly written piece,  work jointly to form simple sentences from a substitution table,  peer assess each other’s sentences for neatness,  rearrange words to make meaningful sentences about locating school facilities,  compose a short essay on the theme neatly and legibly using the prescribed Arabic style.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How do we take care of our school facilities? 2. Why should we write neatly and legibly?
